forest_09_001.speaker: narrator
forest_09_001.text: In the clinic, the boy slept through the morning while his grandmother counted the knots in the spare rope. The assistant had checked him repeatedly overnight. His alertness and warmth had improved, but the toes injured by cold would need time before their recovery could be judged. Lin brought breakfast for the grandmother from the ordinary family-support allotment. The old woman ate standing until the assistant pointed firmly at the chair. Lin recognized the gesture from Shi Lan's lunches.

forest_09_002.speaker: narrator
forest_09_002.text: The boy woke and asked about his bundle. His grandmother said it was home. He asked whether the stove had been lit. She said yes. Only then did he begin crying. Lin went outside while the grandmother held him. The assistant followed to fetch another dry cloth and said the child had been afraid of returning empty-handed. His summer confidence and the household's immediate need had met a winter ditch. Blame would have to wait until warmth had made a conversation possible.

forest_09_003.speaker: narrator
forest_09_003.text: Outside, Wen was splitting ordinary kindling within the clinic's work arrangement. The clinic fuel came from its funded stock, not the boy's recovered bundle. He had offered a paid maintenance turn during the keeper's slack interval and was grateful for work that produced visible pieces. Lin stood beside the stack and read her mother's letter again. Wen asked whether it was good news. She said it was ordinary news, which had made her unexpectedly homesick.

forest_09_004.speaker: lin_yue
forest_09_004.text: She wrote about my cup. There is a place on the shelf where it used to stand. I have been thinking about mountains, foundries, rivers, forests, and how far a fourth-stage field can carry an honest task. She has been looking at a shelf. Neither view cancels the other. I want to visit. I also want to finish the work I accepted here. I am trying not to make the second wish sound noble so I can ignore the first.

forest_09_005.speaker: narrator
forest_09_005.text: Wen put down the splitting tool before answering. His sister lived a short walk away and he still managed to miss meals she wanted him at. Distance was not the only way to be absent. He said Lin could write a proposed visit interval after the commission, with the road and receiving arrangements checked later. She said that sounded sensible and far away. He agreed. The agreement was kind because he did not try to make far away feel near.

forest_09_006.speaker: narrator
forest_09_006.text: At the lodging, Lin wrote a reply before her next shift. She described the child only in general terms, leaving another family's private fear out of the letter. She told her mother she wanted an ordinary visit after the forest commission and would check the actual route before making a date. Then she wrote about Wen's sister's good door, including the first leak in the roof test. The small failure made the story feel more like a house her mother might recognize.

forest_09_007.speaker: narrator
forest_09_007.text: Shi Lan arranged Lin's next paid observation turn near the upper corridor. The district keeper had requested calm reports of the Harts' movements and any speech they offered, rather than attempts to force an examination. Lin had known the orchard visitor's words, not merely its body. She realized she had been treating its silence in the dangerous encounters as if silence erased that personhood. Fear had narrowed her own listening as surely as the loading platform had narrowed the path.

forest_09_008.speaker: narrator
forest_09_008.text: The adult Hart stood beyond the protected bend when Lin and the qualified watch reached their station. Crystal antlers caught weak light among the firs. Dormant buds lay sheltered in their branching hollows, as Lin remembered from the orchard. The younger Hart rested uphill, one root braid draped beside the injured leg. The watch stayed back, leaving an open exit. Lin spoke her name once from the marked distance and waited, her hands empty and visible.

forest_09_009.speaker: frostroot_hart
forest_09_009.text: I remember the room with the copper rest. You were beside the man in the green apron. There is no rest like that here. There is a path, and people keep placing things across it. When the dog came toward the small one, I could not make words arrive before my body moved. You saw the body. Do not tell the village it is gentle. Tell them where it needs room to pass.

forest_09_010.speaker: narrator
forest_09_010.text: The voice was low and rougher than Lin remembered. She answered that the cart and the injured woman had been helped, and the path was now clearer. The Hart listened without lowering its head. The watch recorded only the offered words and visible position. Lin wanted to ask a dozen questions about the snare, the antler dealer, and the small one's leg. She began with whether the current protected turn was usable. The answer would change something they could actually do.

forest_09_011.speaker: frostroot_hart
forest_09_011.text: The upper bend is usable while the branches remain lifted. The cold water lies across the lower one. The small one can walk, but cannot step quickly where the ice breaks. We need the shallow bank beyond the resting tree. People gather there when the sun reaches it. I do not ask that they leave every tree to us. I ask that they see two bodies coming before they fill the only bank we can cross.

forest_09_012.speaker: narrator
forest_09_012.text: Shi Lan had reached the observation point by then, staying behind Lin. She asked whether a marked quiet interval would help if gatherers used the bank at different hours. The Hart said it might, provided people did not arrive early and wait inside the narrow approach. The detail mattered. A schedule could appear to separate uses while placing a queue exactly where the animal needed space. Shi Lan sketched the waiting point farther down, where the path widened.

forest_09_013.speaker: frostroot_hart
forest_09_013.text: The small one's leg hurts where the iron closed. I pulled until the root broke free. I do not know the man who placed it. I smelled his smoke later above the hollow. Many people smell of smoke. I cannot give you a name from that. The hand that made the loop need not be the hand that left the pot. Ask your own witnesses. I will tell you what touched us, and no more.

forest_09_014.speaker: narrator
forest_09_014.text: Lin thanked the Hart for the account and asked whether the district keeper's assistant could observe the leg again from the high bank. The Hart agreed to that distance and declined a close approach today. The observation could proceed under the field plan without pretending to be treatment. Lin felt disappointment rise, then fade when she saw the youngster turn its head toward them. The adult's refusal was not a puzzle she had been hired to solve.

forest_09_015.speaker: narrator
forest_09_015.text: The younger Hart lifted itself slowly and moved toward the shallow bank. The adult followed, keeping its antlers between the youngster and the people. Lin stepped back with the watch as planned. She could now recognize the movement as both protective intention and dangerous force. Knowing the intention did not make standing in its way sensible. The pair crossed the clear stretch and disappeared among the reeds. A dormant bud had fallen beside the track, pale green inside its crystal dust.

forest_09_016.speaker: narrator
forest_09_016.text: The watch left the bud where it lay and noted its position for the habitat keeper. Lin did not bring it back as a token. The orchard's visitor had returned to being someone with work and fear beyond her own story. She carried the offered passage request to Shi Lan and the council. The animal account would join the human observations as testimony from a particular place, not serve as a magical map of every unseen act in the forest.

forest_09_017.speaker: shi_lan
forest_09_017.text: We can move the gathering wait to the lower widening and give the shallow bank a short protected crossing interval. The paid carriers can still collect at the wide turn. I want the affected households asked today, before the watch changes tomorrow's arrangement. The Hart has told us one useful thing: our queue was blocking the space even when nobody had entered the path. The human watch could have noticed that too. We will not wait for antlers to explain every bottleneck.

forest_09_018.speaker: narrator
forest_09_018.text: The gathering households reviewed the proposed waiting point. Most accepted it. The elderly man with the difficult knees asked whether he would have to stand downhill longer. Shi Lan arranged seating at the wider shelter and kept his named carrying turn. Another woman objected that the crossing interval overlapped her usual work start. The council offered the earlier carrier slot then available, and she accepted. No one needed to claim the Hart's request had made every human schedule simple.

forest_09_019.speaker: narrator
forest_09_019.text: At the clinic that evening, the boy asked Lin whether the Hart had been angry with him. She said he had not met it on the path; his accident involved the hidden ditch. He looked relieved and then ashamed. His grandmother told him being afraid of a thing did not mean that thing had caused every bad event nearby. Lin smiled at the familiar lesson arriving from an older voice. The boy asked whether the Hart could speak. She said yes, when it wanted and felt able.

forest_09_020.speaker: narrator
forest_09_020.text: He wanted to hear it someday. The assistant said someday could wait until his toes and ankle allowed the ordinary walk, and the watch found a suitable calm opportunity. The boy accepted the delay more readily than any adult at the burn meeting had. His grandmother gave him a spoonful of soup and told him the immediate ambition was finishing the bowl. Lin left before the conversation became another promise she might not be able to keep.

forest_09_021.speaker: narrator
forest_09_021.text: Outside, the evening snow was light enough to hear individual flakes touch the dry reeds near the path. Wen waited with two cups. He asked what the Hart had said. Lin told him the offered account, including its inability to name the snare maker. Wen listened, then looked toward the forest. He said he had wanted the animal to be either a victim they could save or a danger they could remove. It had inconveniently become a neighbor who could complain about the queue.

forest_09_022.speaker: narrator
forest_09_022.text: On the third clinic morning, the boy's toes looked less frightening and hurt more. The assistant explained that changing pain did not by itself tell them how the damaged skin would heal. The boy asked whether he could walk by the marriage feast. His grandmother had told him about Wen's sister's date to give him something beyond the bed. The assistant said they would decide from the actual foot, not the invitation. He frowned at his foot as if it had become discourteous.

forest_09_023.speaker: narrator
forest_09_023.text: His grandmother wanted to take him home as soon as possible. The clinic's emergency support covered the immediate care, but she had other household tasks and a stove to tend. A neighbor had helped twice already. Lin asked what would make the next days manageable. The grandmother said another load of dry wood would help more than another cup of tea. Lin stopped offering tea. The access desk arranged the family's existing allotted bundle through the revised carrier turn.

forest_09_024.speaker: narrator
forest_09_024.text: The boy's mother arrived from her paid lower-settlement work after receiving the message. She had negotiated two days away and brought his wool scarf, which he had refused on the morning he left. She put it beside the bed without scolding him. Later, outside the screen, she cried while the grandmother described the ditch. Lin kept walking to the water station because the family had not asked for an audience. The scarf stayed beside the pillow, silently more persuasive than any rebuke.

forest_09_025.speaker: narrator
forest_09_025.text: Long came to ask whether the carrier arrangements were working with the spare cart. The mother asked him about the credit terms if she missed more work to remain at the clinic. Long said the ordinary revised plan required actual repayment capacity; he would not pretend an absent wage was one. He directed her to the council's hardship review and offered the existing short collection hold where her household already had an account. She looked angry, then relieved that no new loan had been pushed into the silence.

forest_09_026.speaker: long_qian
forest_09_026.text: I can supply grain for sale and a limited credit plan. The council can decide its relief. I will give it the household's relevant current balance if you permit, and nothing about other purchases it does not need. I know this sounds like handing you another desk. I wish I had an answer that did not. I can walk to that desk with you now, after you have finished speaking to the assistant. You should not have to explain the same missed wage badly three times.

forest_09_027.speaker: narrator
forest_09_027.text: He accompanied her. The clerk accepted the actual wage interruption and assessed the household under the existing hardship allowance, granting a bounded food portion for the next interval. It did not replace all the missed earnings. The mother read the amount and asked when review occurred if the boy remained unable to walk. The clerk gave the date. Long waited until the exchange finished. On leaving, he carried the grain to the family cart without turning the act into a concession in his price argument.

forest_09_028.speaker: narrator
forest_09_028.text: Lin found herself remembering the orchard couches. Pain could be moved there under qualified treatment, sometimes, while injury remained. The wild Hart had once accepted that work. For a brief, shameful moment she imagined asking it to help the boy, as if a speaking creature nearby made the forest into another treatment room. Then she pictured the injured youngster and the adult's urgent crossing request. The thought did not deserve a plan merely because it contained compassion.

forest_09_029.speaker: lin_yue
forest_09_029.text: I remembered a relief method from somewhere else and almost treated remembering as a reason to propose it here. The clinic has no qualified exchange circuit for this treatment, and the Hart is caring for its own injured young one. What I can offer today is the washing turn and the ordinary route account. That feels smaller than what I wanted to offer. I am learning that the feeling is not a command. Please give me the cloths that actually need washing.

forest_09_030.speaker: narrator
forest_09_030.text: The assistant gave her a full basin. By the time Lin carried the clean cloths to dry, her wish for a larger cure had become fatigue in her elbows. The boy called from the bed, asking whether she had seen the paper dog. Wen had promised to bring it if the niece agreed to lend it. Lin said she had not yet seen today's visitor list. The boy laughed at the grand phrase. His mother smiled for the first time since arriving.

forest_09_031.speaker: narrator
forest_09_031.text: The niece agreed to lend the dog for one afternoon and accompanied it as guardian. Shi Lan brought her during the clinic's permitted family visiting interval. The child approached the bed quietly after receiving the assistant's instructions. She introduced the dog by explaining its tether improvements, then asked the boy whether his toes were still angry. He said very. She said the dog would not step on them. Lin watched a conversation succeed because neither child tried to make it profound.

forest_09_032.speaker: narrator
forest_09_032.text: Outside, Shi Lan asked the mother whether she wanted the route review to include the boy's own account later. The mother said yes when he felt ready, and wanted the ditch inspected now. The ditch had drained onto a hollow under old boards, which snow concealed. Its summer crossing had never been designed for winter gathering loads. The district path worker would examine it with the council, keeping the barrier in place meanwhile. The mother's face sharpened at the word never.

forest_09_033.speaker: narrator
forest_09_033.text: She said everyone had used that shortcut for years. Shi Lan said the review would record that use instead of pretending the closed board erased it. The grandfather of another household came forward to confirm how often people crossed in summer. Pei joined the discussion with the old winter passage map. The unsafe shortcut and the retained passage were different routes. Their names had become confused in village speech, just as the land and road markers had. Lin felt the inquiry's next knot tightening.

forest_09_034.speaker: pei_yun
forest_09_034.text: We have called three paths the low way. In summer, everyone points and understands. In winter, a child carrying wood hears the name and follows the memory he has. I can put the proper route names on the new map. I should also put the old common names beneath them, or people will see a tidy sheet describing roads they do not recognize. The office has been very good at preserving words and less good at asking where they send feet.

forest_09_035.speaker: narrator
forest_09_035.text: The path worker found the old ditch boards rotten beneath the snow. They had not failed under the boy; he had stepped beside them where water undercut the edge. Repairing the boards alone would leave that edge dangerous. The council accepted a temporary winter closure and a longer-term drainage and crossing repair proposal, to be funded separately before work. The wider route would carry the current gathering turn. The boy's mother listened without being asked to admire how thorough everyone had become afterward.

forest_09_036.speaker: narrator
forest_09_036.text: That evening, she told Lin she had wanted to shout at the warden. Lin said she understood. The mother asked whether understanding meant she thought the warden had caused the accident. Lin said no; it meant a frightened parent might need somewhere to put the question before evidence answered it. The mother sat silently. Then she said she would bring the question to the review and try not to bring every cruel sentence she had invented during the walk up from the lower settlement.

forest_09_037.speaker: narrator
forest_09_037.text: The boy slept while his mother and grandmother ate together. Neither could return to work immediately, and neither had a complete plan for the next fortnight. The bounded food portion helped. The neighbor's stove help helped. The clinic's paid family support turn helped. Together these small arrangements formed a fragile bridge over days nobody had budgeted for. Lin left the room knowing the bridge existed, not knowing whether the foot would recover without lasting loss. Both thoughts stayed with her through supper.

forest_09_038.speaker: narrator
forest_09_038.text: At the lodging, Wen's sister was deciding which blanket to bring into the new house. The best one belonged to the family and had warmed three generations through bad roofs. She wanted it, then felt greedy for wanting it. Her intended husband offered his thinner blanket as exchange until they could buy another. The uncle said she could simply take the good one. Wen asked whether the remaining household would be warm enough. The answer required looking at actual bedding, not at how generous everybody sounded.

forest_09_039.speaker: narrator
forest_09_039.text: They laid the blankets on the floor and counted the sleeping places. The older house had another heavy quilt stored in a chest, unused because its cover needed mending. Lin offered a sewing afternoon within her rest time, then withdrew the offer when the basket mender's niece said she had already been hired for that mend. The solution had existed before Lin entered the room. She smiled, feeling slightly foolish, and helped fold the quilt for its appointed repair.

forest_09_040.speaker: wen_cai
forest_09_040.text: You looked relieved when someone else had the job. Then you looked ashamed of being relieved. I am becoming an expert in your sequence of expressions. That may be a dangerous profession. My sister says you do not need to carry every basin in order to remain welcome at the table. I agree with her this time. Sit down. The potatoes are not going to inspect your employment history before deciding whether you may eat them.

forest_09_041.speaker: narrator
forest_09_041.text: Lin sat. The uncle passed the pickle bowl. Wen's sister asked about the boy's recovery, and Lin gave only the public condition the family had permitted them to share: improving overall, still under care for the foot and ankle. The conversation moved to the marriage meal. Pei's missing romantic verse had become a subject of great strategic interest. The intended husband said he would sing it badly if necessary. His bride told him she had known the risk when accepting him.

forest_09_042.speaker: narrator
forest_09_042.text: After dinner, Lin walked the short path to the lodging with her mother's reply inside her coat. She had not yet fixed a visit date beyond the commission. She had sent a real wish and a plan to check the route, which felt both inadequate and honest. In the sky above the forest, clouds covered the stars one ridge at a time. The hollow was dark. Somewhere within it, a root-maned mother watched an injured child of her own, under a winter no letter could soften.

forest_09_043.speaker: narrator
forest_09_043.text: The clinic's next report allowed the boy to sit upright longer and begin the advised gentle movement, but kept weight off the damaged foot. His mother asked whether the skin would scar. The assistant said it might; the extent remained uncertain. The boy listened from the pillow and asked whether a scar would make his boot rub. His grandmother fetched the boot, which was too small already. Winter had hidden a growing child's need inside an old familiar pair.

forest_09_044.speaker: narrator
forest_09_044.text: The council equipment allowance covered work boots, not every child's footwear. The mother knew this and had not asked it to. Wen's sister knew a cobbler who accepted paid mending work in exchange for a plain larger pair. She gave the family the ordinary quoted arrangement, and the mother chose it after considering her available hours. It was useful advice from someone who had negotiated her own small household repairs. Lin listened, taking care not to turn every exchange into a personal rescue.

forest_09_045.speaker: narrator
forest_09_045.text: At the gathering shelter, the new early carrier turns worked through the hard-frost morning. The elderly woman who had moved the fire flag came with her grandson and waited at the lower widening. He pointed toward the resting tree and asked whether the Hart liked it. She said the Hart could answer for itself if it wished; she liked the tree because her husband had sat there. The boy accepted two uses for one patch of shade more readily than several adults had.

forest_09_046.speaker: narrator
forest_09_046.text: Shi Lan checked the quiet crossing interval with the watch. The adult Hart appeared at its edge, then waited while the last gathering group passed. The watch kept the path open rather than advancing toward it. When the people cleared, the pair crossed the shallow bank. The younger Hart moved stiffly but did not fall. The adult's crystal branches brushed the resting tree. One bud opened a fraction in the protected hollow of an antler, pale as a thought before words.

forest_09_047.speaker: frostroot_hart
forest_09_047.text: The waiting place is better. Today I could hear the people before I had to move. I cannot promise every crossing will be quiet. The small one wakes frightened when its leg catches a reed. I wake frightened with it. There is room for that fear here now. Tell the woman who kept her child back that I saw her. Tell the dog keeper to keep the dog close. I have no wish to carry another cart rail.

forest_09_048.speaker: narrator
forest_09_048.text: The watch recorded the offered thanks and warning. Lin delivered them at the shelter, where the dog owner looked embarrassed and showed the new tether. The woman with the child said she was pleased the animal had noticed, though she would prefer never to be noticed by antlers at close range. Shi Lan agreed. A shared arrangement had begun to work without requiring shared affection. Lin found this less disappointing now that she had seen fear from both sides of the path.

forest_09_049.speaker: narrator
forest_09_049.text: The preliminary burn readings remained outside the accepted window. The crew continued authorized maintenance and billet handling, with no ignition callout. The senior worker's kettle acquired a knitted sleeve from the basket mender's family. It looked ridiculous and kept the water liquid longer. Wen asked whether the sleeve was a promotion. The worker said it was an intimate professional partnership and none of Wen's business. Shi Lan laughed so hard that the niece demanded to know which word had caused it.

forest_09_050.speaker: narrator
forest_09_050.text: The road crossing passed its qualified final checks and reopened at the posted load limit after the drainage work and support replacement. The road office notified the quotation supplier directly. A revised winter offer would still need current stock, receiving condition, price, and route dates confirmed. Rong read the notice with relief and resisted announcing that the original extra fuel was now secured. Long saw him resisting and said the restraint looked painful. Rong replied that he was developing new muscles.

forest_09_051.speaker: narrator
forest_09_051.text: Their banter ended when the outside supplier's reply came. Its earlier limited stock had partly been sold during the closure; only a smaller quantity remained available at the current price. The reopening restored a route, not the vanished inventory. The proposal stayed useful but insufficient to cover every possible loss. Long wanted to reserve it immediately. Rong wanted to compare its deposit terms first. The old competition returned across the office table, more informed and no less real.

forest_09_052.speaker: long_qian
forest_09_052.text: If we spend three days comparing every line, someone else will buy the remaining bags. If we pay a deposit before verifying the stock, we may buy a letter instead of fuel. I know both risks. I am tired of discovering that knowing them does not choose between them. Pei, can the receiving agent inspect today? If that inspection has a price, give us the price. I would like to purchase one actual fact before we purchase another promise.

forest_09_053.speaker: narrator
forest_09_053.text: The licensed receiving agent could inspect the supplier's current stack the next morning for an agreed fee split by the interested buyers. The council did not pay the commercial reservation fee. Rong and Long authorized the inspection from their business funds, asking for dry condition and existing commitments, not merely a visible pile. Lin carried the request to the courier desk within her assigned message turn. She did not travel to the supplier herself just because the task sounded more adventurous than bowls.

forest_09_054.speaker: narrator
forest_09_054.text: At the courier desk, a town packet arrived for Pei. The land inspector would come in the seventh commission week with the original docket references and a qualified field assistant. The purported northern confirmation's seal differed from the issued version in a small missing notch, but the comparison was still being documented. Its author remained unknown. Pei stared at the packet until Lin asked whether she should call Shi Lan. The keeper said not yet, then changed her mind and said yes.

forest_09_055.speaker: narrator
forest_09_055.text: Shi Lan read the visit notice and asked Pei what else the survey needed. Pei said the surviving lower marker base and the second fixed point would have to be checked against the older line. The warden asked about the missing top of the broken marker. Pei's face closed. She said floods carried stone strangely. Shi Lan said this stone had been carved and heavy. Pei asked whether she was being accused. The room became quiet enough to hear the clerk's brush pause.

forest_09_056.speaker: shi_lan
forest_09_056.text: I am asking where it went because you watched the road work and have kept these records longer than anyone. You may not know. If you know part, give us that part. The next survey should not spend a day searching the wrong bank because we are all protecting an old story. I am not afraid of discovering your memory is incomplete. I am afraid of discovering you had a useful fact and decided we could not bear it.

forest_09_057.speaker: narrator
forest_09_057.text: Pei turned toward the window. Beyond it, the gate's winter board had been moved farther back at the gatherers' request. A small practical correction stood where everyone could see it. Lin thought the keeper would answer. Instead, Pei said she needed to check something before speaking. Shi Lan accepted a short stated interval, with the inspector's visit unchanged. Pei left through the rear door. The clerk resumed writing, too carefully. Lin felt the office's familiar furniture become unfamiliar around her.

forest_09_058.speaker: narrator
forest_09_058.text: That afternoon, Lin worked at the kiln with Wen. He noticed her silence and asked whether the mother letter had become difficult again. She said the boundary inquiry had. He wanted details; she gave the public visit date and said Pei was checking an additional fact. Wen respected the limit and looked worried anyway. His foreman's unauthorized cut had followed the very confusion Pei might know more about. A keeper's hesitation could reach a crewman's future without his being in the room.

forest_09_059.speaker: narrator
forest_09_059.text: Rong received the supplier inspection terms and the land-visit notice in the same hour. He looked from one to the other and said town businessmen thought forests were slow because they saw only the papers after the walking. Lin said some of the slowness came from papers too. He nodded and opened the current stock report. Accepted kiln output continued on schedule within the conservative plan so far. The pending northern question remained excluded. He did not let possible permission inflate the report.

forest_09_060.speaker: narrator
forest_09_060.text: At dusk, the boy's mother returned to her lower-settlement job after arranging her grandmother's support and the clinic's next review. She hated leaving. The boy promised to remain in bed, then asked whether she could bring a larger boot. She said they were arranging it. Their goodbye was less dramatic than the first arrival and more difficult. Lin stayed outside with the folded scarf, which the mother had forgotten in her haste. She delivered it before the cart left.

forest_09_061.speaker: narrator
forest_09_061.text: The mother pressed the scarf to her face and thanked Lin. Then she gave it back for the boy, laughing at herself. The cart moved down the clear road while she looked over her shoulder until the bend took the clinic away. Lin watched the empty stretch afterward. Her own mother's shelf returned to mind, painfully specific. She could not turn the forest commission into an excuse never to visit. She also could not make a visit occur by staring south.

forest_09_062.speaker: narrator
forest_09_062.text: That night she practiced only after eating and resting. The paired fourth-stage sequence steadied on the second attempt, then degraded when she tried to extend beyond her planned turn. She discharged and stopped. Wen, mending a sack nearby, said she looked annoyed with the air. She said she had wanted one thing that would improve simply by wanting harder. He held up his crooked seam and said the thread shared no such policy. They both returned to the slower method.

forest_09_063.speaker: narrator
forest_09_063.text: Near midnight, Pei knocked at the lodging door. She carried a wrapped object heavy enough to strain both hands. Shi Lan rose without waking the child. Lin followed them to the table, where the keeper set the bundle down and unfolded its cloth. A carved stone corner lay inside, stained dark along one broken edge. Pei said it belonged to the old marker. She had kept it eleven years. The room's warmth seemed to withdraw from the space around her.

forest_09_064.speaker: pei_yun
forest_09_064.text: I found it after the flood, when the road crew cleared the lower setting. It has my father's witness mark on the side. The new marker was already upright above the cart turn, and people were pleased to have a road that did not disappear beneath water. I took the broken corner home before it went into the rubble pile. I told myself it was a keepsake. Then I let the keepsake become a fact nobody else could inspect.

forest_09_065.speaker: narrator
forest_09_065.text: Shi Lan leaned over the stone without touching it. Lin recognized the little mark Pei had once mistaken for a bird in her father's handwriting. Beneath it, a short alignment groove survived along the broken edge. The fragment might help identify the original marker's orientation if it fitted the base, subject to the inspector's examination. Pei had not merely kept a sentimental stone. She had withheld something useful while everyone walked around her incomplete account.

forest_09_066.speaker: lin_yue
forest_09_066.text: You asked me to distinguish a memory, a document, and a stone. I have repeated that lesson to other people. You had part of the stone. I am trying to ask the useful question first, and I am angry enough that the other questions keep getting in its way. Where has this piece been kept? Who else saw it? Has anyone tried to fit it to the base since you took it? We need those answers before tomorrow becomes another day built around what you have not said.

forest_09_067.speaker: narrator
forest_09_067.text: Pei answered slowly. The fragment had stayed in the locked survey drawer for eleven years, apart from occasional private examination. Her nephew had seen it when helping move the cabinet years earlier; he had not known its role. Nobody had fitted it to the base since the flood. Pei said she had feared the old line would make the rebuilt cart approach seem unlawful, cutting off the household access everyone had come to rely on. The road order had disproved that fear days ago.

forest_09_068.speaker: pei_yun
forest_09_068.text: After we found the order, I should have brought this out immediately. Instead, I was ashamed of how long I had waited. Shame is excellent at finding one more reason to wait. I thought the second survey might settle the line without anyone learning what was in my drawer. When Shi Lan asked today, I heard myself giving the river the blame for a stone I could have put on the desk. That was when I finally stopped pretending the silence was practical.

forest_09_069.speaker: narrator
forest_09_069.text: The niece stirred in her bedding, and Shi Lan lowered her voice. She said Pei would need to give the account to the land inspector and the public office, with the fragment's custody history. Pei agreed. Lin wanted to demand why a keeper devoted to correct records had chosen this particular concealment. The answer was already partly on the table: love for a father, fear for a road, pride in being the person everyone consulted. None excused the delay. Together they made it harder to dismiss her as merely dishonest.

forest_09_070.speaker: shi_lan
forest_09_070.text: Tonight we will secure it where the inspector can examine it under recorded custody. Tomorrow you will make your account before the office changes any boundary claim. I will accompany you if you still want company. The people who relied on your incomplete answer may be angry. Do not arrive prepared to persuade them they should not be. Bring what you know and the thing you kept. That is enough work for one morning.

forest_09_071.speaker: narrator
forest_09_071.text: Pei asked for company. Shi Lan accepted, then wrapped the fragment in a clean cloth with Lin witnessing the pack and date. The old keeper looked relieved and devastated in equal measure. When she left, the lodging seemed too quiet. Lin stood by the stove, angry at having learned a lesson from someone who had not followed it. Shi Lan said that happened often enough to be ordinary, but it was still allowed to hurt. Lin wished the ordinary things would stop arriving so heavily.

forest_09_072.speaker: narrator
forest_09_072.text: Wen had heard only the voices, not the whole account. Lin gave him the public plan for tomorrow after Pei permitted that fact to be shared: an additional marker fragment and the keeper's custody statement would go to the inspector. He looked toward the office. He said his foreman would ask whether Pei's silence changed the unauthorized cut. Lin said the land office would decide the actual boundary; withholding evidence did not automatically license every earlier act. She hoped she had not made the sentence too tidy for its consequences.

forest_09_073.speaker: narrator
forest_09_073.text: Before dawn, the clinic sent a short message that the boy had slept well and the foot's current condition remained stable under observation. The news reached a room holding a wrapped stone, two angry adults, and a child still asleep beside paper antlers. Lin read it aloud. The niece woke at the last line and asked whether stable meant he could race. Shi Lan said no. Wen said it meant the race could remain a future argument. The child found that acceptable.

forest_09_074.speaker: narrator
forest_09_074.text: Pei arrived for the office walk wearing her oldest coat. Lin thought she looked smaller, then realized she had stopped arranging herself like a keeper about to receive visitors. She was now a witness bringing an uncomfortable fact. Shi Lan took the wrapped fragment. Lin carried the date copy. Outside, the clear path led past the good-door house, where a thin thread of smoke rose from the working stove. The cart road remained useful. The old stone would have to tell a different story.

forest_09_075.speaker: narrator
forest_09_075.text: The land inspector reached the gate before their group did, delayed less than expected by the reopened crossing. He had the current docket, the certified old road order, and a spare pair of boots tied to his case. Pei stopped beside the gatepost and told him she had additional physical evidence and a withheld custody history. He listened without welcoming or condemning her. Then he asked for a dry table and the full account. The seventh week's boundary survey began with the keeper no longer keeping the most useful thing alone.
